items.title: Luna Agent – Custom AI agent in ~2300 lines of Python, no frameworks
items.raw_excerpt:
Hey HN. I evaluated three agent frameworks for a homelab project, one had 400K lines of code (and 42K exposed instances on Shodan), one was 9 days old, and the third was so thin I'd rebuild most of it anyway. None worked for me. So I built my own in ~2300 lines of Python. No frameworks, 8 runtime dependencies, 106 tests. What it does:
- Persistent memory via SQLite (FTS5 keyword search + sqlite-vec embeddings + recency decay, fused with Reciprocal Rank Fusion)
- MCP tool integration — add capabilities by editing a JSON file
- Native tools with safety guardrails (bash blocklist, timeouts, output caps)
- Discord interface with session isolation
- Structured JSON logging for every operation
- Conversation compression for effectively infinite context Runs locally on 2x RTX 3090 with Qwen3-Code

title_i18n.es: Luna Agent – Agente de IA personalizado en aproximadamente 2300 líneas de Python, sin frameworks

excerpt_i18n.en:

I evaluated three agent frameworks for a homelab project, one had 400K lines of code (and 42K exposed instances on Shodan), one was 9 days old, and the third was so thin I'd rebuild most of it anyway. None worked for me. So I built my own in ~2300 lines of Python. No frameworks, 8 runtime dependencies, 106 tests. What it does:
- Persistent memory via SQLite (FTS5 keyword search + sqlite-vec embeddings + recency decay, fused with Reciprocal Rank Fusion)
- MCP tool integration — add capabilities by editing a JSON file
- Native tools with safety guardrails (bash blocklist, timeouts, output caps)
- Discord interface with session isolation
- Structured JSON logging for every operation
- Conversation compression for effectively infinite context Runs locally on 2x RTX 3090 with Qwen3-Code
excerpt_i18n.zh: 各位HN网友，我在一个家庭实验室项目中评估了三款智能体框架：其中一个代码量达40万行（且在Shodan上暴露了4.2万个实例），另一个仅发布9天，第三个则过于简陋，我基本需要重构大部分功能。最终无一可用。

items.title: AICurate – AI news curation platform for associations
items.raw_excerpt: AICurate lets professional associations create AI-curated news hubs for their members. Problem: Associations spend 10-15 hrs/week manually finding, filtering, and summarizing industry news for members. Solution: Configure industries, topics, and RSS/web sources. AI agent scans, scores relevance, generates summaries, and delivers via branded portal + email digests. Multi-tenant architecture, each org gets isolated config, branding, and analytics. Curation AI is configurable per-tenant so a legal association and a medical society can have completely different relevance criteria. Currently handles RSS feeds and web source discovery. Working on adding direct API integrations with major news providers.

The financial side covers market primitives (orderbook, OHLCV, indicators, position, risk) and a streaming ingestion pipeline handling 100K+ ticks/second across 4 exchanges. Everything is zero-panic enforced at the lint level, typed errors

The author argues that current AI systems are approaching the limits of Shannon's framework, while Kolmogorov's theory reveals fundamental constraints in creativity, intuition, and genuine understanding.

title_i18n.es: Shannon llevó a la IA hasta aquí. Kolmogorov muestra dónde se detiene.

items.title: NervOS – Sandbox for AI Agents Using Firecracker MicroVMs
items.raw_excerpt: I built NervOS to safely run AI agent code inside a Firecracker microVM instead of directly on the host machine. It boots a lightweight Alpine VM and provides tools like Python, bash, curl and git for the agent to use. If something goes wrong, the VM can be destroyed and the host remains untouched. Currently experimenting with using it alongside MCP for local agents. Repo: https://github.com/ashishgituser/NervOS Docs: https://ashishgituser.github.io/NervOS/

items.title: TracePact – Catch tool-call regressions in AI agents before prod
items.raw_excerpt: I kept running into the same problem: I'd change a prompt or update my model, the agent output looked fine, but the tool sequence was completely different. It stopped reading config before deploying. It ran npm run build instead of npm test . The bug showed up days later in prod. So I built TracePact. Record a known-good run as a cassette, diff against new runs, get a clear report of what changed: - read_file (seq 0) (removed) ~ bash.cmd: "npm test" -> "npm run build" Summary: 1 removed, 1 arg changed[BLOCK] It classifies changes as block (structural) or warn (args only), so you can gate CI with --fail-on warn. You can filter noise with --ignore-keys timestamp and --ignore-tools read_file. No API calls needed for replay/diff. Works with any LLM provider. Vitest integration for writing asse

title_i18n.en: TracePact – Catch tool-call regressions in AI agents before prod
title_i18n.zh: TracePact——在AI代理投入生产前捕捉工具调用回归问题
title_i18n.es: TracePact – Detecta regresiones en llamadas a herramientas en agentes de IA antes de producción

You can filter noise with --ignore-keys timestamp and --ignore-tools read_file. No API calls needed for replay/diff. Works with any LLM provider. Vitest integration for writing asse

items.title: SafeAgent – exactly-once execution guard for AI agent side effects
items.raw_excerpt:
I built a small Python library called SafeAgent that protects real-world side effects when AI agents retry tool calls. One issue we ran into while experimenting with agent workflows is that retries can trigger irreversible actions multiple times: agent calls tool
↓
network timeout
↓
agent retries
↓
side effect happens twice Examples: • duplicate payment
• duplicate email
• duplicate ticket
• duplicate trade Most systems solve this ad-hoc using idempotency keys scattered around different services. SafeAgent centralizes this into a small execution guard. The idea is simple: 1. every tool execution gets a request_id
2. SafeAgent records the execution receipt
3. retries return the original receipt instead of running the side effect again Example: FIRST CALL
REAL SIDE EFFECT: sending email SECO

title_i18n.zh: SafeAgent——AI代理副作用的一次性执行保障器。

excerpt_i18n.en:
On March 7, the "Visibility Growth Summit," jointly organized by Yeahmobi, Feifan Industrial Research, Similarweb, and Tencent Cloud, successfully concluded in Nanshan, Shenzhen. Focusing on the core of brand growth in the AI era, the summit brought together leading forces in global digital marketing, including AppLovin, Shopify, Moloco, impact.com, and Zhipu AI. It systematically shared actionable AI growth methodologies for practitioners such as brand founders, overseas expansion strategists, and growth leaders, exploring how brands can build core "visibility capabilities" in the intelligent age.  

Guided by practical application, the summit featured three specialized sessions: "Visibility × Search," "Visibility × Advertising," and "Visibility × Agent." Through keynote speeches and in-depth roundtable discussions, it systematically presented practical pathways for brands to build visibility capabilities in the AI era, covering dimensions such as generative search optimization, AI advertising automation, and intelligent agent business strategies. This provided actionable guidance for enterprises to break through growth bottlenecks and seize algorithmic dividends.  

The summit also released the "2026 Global AI Marketing Trends and Value White Paper," jointly initiated by Yeahmobi and Alibaba Cloud, with participation from industry pioneers such as Google, PubMatic, BIGO Ads, Smadex, Adjust, Salesforce, Crazy Maple Studio, Jetour Automobile, realme, Pixel Bloom, Huxiu Think Tank, and Yangfan Chuhai.
excerpt_i18n.es: El 7 de marzo, la Cumbre de Crecimiento de Visibilidad, organizada conjuntamente por Yeahmobi, Feifan Industrial Research, Similarweb y Tencent Cloud, concluyó con éxito en Nanshan, Shenzhen. Centrándose en el núcleo del crecimiento de marcas en la era de la IA, esta cumbre reunió a líderes globales en marketing digital como AppLovin, Shopify, Moloco, impact.com y Zhipu AI, compartiendo sistemáticamente metodologías prácticas de crecimiento con IA para fundadores de marcas, responsables de expansión internacional y líderes de crecimiento, y explorando cómo las marcas pueden construir capacidades centrales de visibilidad en la era inteligente. Orientada a la práctica, la cumbre incluyó la sesión Visibilidad × Búsqueda.
